questions.question: When making a normal stop, you should:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use only the rear brake to save the front brake for emergencies.
Use only the front brake to save the rear brake for emergencies.
Squeeze the front brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Get used to using both brakes every time you slow down or stop. If you need to stop quickly, use both brakes. Practicing this habit now makes it easier to do in an emergency.

questions.question: When riding through a curve, a group of motorcyclists should:

options.text: Ride in a staggered formation.
Ride in a single-file formation.
Ride side by side.
Use both lanes if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file formation.
questions.explanation: While staggered formation is normally good, riders should switch to single-file when going through curves, turning, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: To lean a motorcycle when turning, you should:

options.text: Always press the left handgrip.
Always press the right handgrip.
Press the handgrip opposite the direction you are turning.
Press the handgrip in the direction you are turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you are turning.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. To make the motorcycle lean, press on the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, motorcycle riders should look over their shoulders because:

options.text: Motorcycles have blind spots like other vehicles.
Other drivers can see you turning your head.
Mirrors do not work well.
You need to make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots that you cannot see in your mirrors. Always look over your shoulder to check for vehicles or hazards in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: To work well, a face shield should not:

options.text: Have scratches.
Block your side vision.
Be airtight.
Come loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be airtight.
questions.explanation: A good face shield should be scratch-free, hard to break, let you see both sides clearly, fasten tightly, and allow air to pass through. Air flow is important because an airtight shield fogs up and makes it hard to see.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, make sure it is all of the following, except:

options.text: Approved by the U.S. Department of Transportation.
Fits snugly.
Has no damage.
Looks nice.

questions.correctAnswerText: Looks nice.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation and state safety standards, fits snugly all the way around, and has no visible damage such as cracks, loose padding, or torn straps.

questions.question: Passing and being passed on a motorcycle is similar to a car. However:

options.text: Being seen is more important on a motorcycle than a car.
Being seen is less important on a motorcycle than a car.
You should pass on the road shoulder instead of the main road.
It is important to look at other drivers in the eye.

questions.correctAnswerText: Being seen is more important on a motorcycle than a car.
questions.explanation: The basics of passing safely are the same as in a car. However, being visible is more critical on a motorcycle. Because motorcycles are smaller, other drivers may not see you, and you can easily hide in their blind spots.

questions.question: How can you prevent other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Weave back and forth in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to keep other drivers from trying to share it with you.

questions.question: Before each ride, check all of the following, except:

options.text: Fluids.
Headlight and taillight.
Turn signals.
Reflectors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reflectors.
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, taillight, turn signals, brake light, clutch and throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: Under normal road and traffic conditions, keep at least a ______ following distance.

options.text: One-second
Two-second
Three-second
Four-second

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-second
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, keep at least a two-second gap between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance when road or weather conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: During a normal turn, what should happen?

options.text: The motorcycle and rider should lean at the same angle.
The motorcycle and rider should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should lean, but the rider should stay upright.
The rider should lean, but the motorcycle should stay upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider should lean at the same angle.
questions.explanation: During normal turns, lean together with your motorcycle at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: A person is legally intoxicated when their blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is at least ______.

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.08 percent
0.1 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: In Kentucky, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means you are legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to drive while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: If you must ride over an obstacle, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down as much as possible.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Speed up if you can.
Stay seated and take your feet off the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as much as possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down and hit it at about a 90-degree angle. Keep your motorcycle upright if possible. Just before impact, ease off the throttle to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning sign
Service sign
Regulatory sign
Speed limit sign

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a safe way to prevent fatigue while riding?

options.text: Protecting yourself from wind, cold, and rain
Taking artificial stimulants
Limiting how far you ride in one day
Taking frequent breaks

questions.correctAnswerText: Taking artificial stimulants
questions.explanation: On long trips, take frequent breaks and ride no more than six hours in one day. Dress to protect yourself from the elements. Do not use artificial stimulants because the dangers increase when they wear off.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection with a stop sign, what should you do?

options.text: Stop at the sign and proceed through the intersection.
Ignore the sign and move forward to see better.
Stop at the sign, move forward slightly, then stop again to see cross traffic better.
Proceed through without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the sign, move forward slightly, then stop again to see cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, first stop at the stop line. Then edge forward and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger in a sidecar, what should you do?

options.text: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
Start slowing down later than usual.
Brake harder than usual to stop quickly.
Brake gently to avoid overusing the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger in a sidecar adds weight and changes how your motorcycle handles. You will need extra space to stop completely.

questions.question: Why is a flat front tire especially dangerous?

options.text: It affects your steering.
The front tire provides power, so you lose acceleration.
It will shake the bike and make mirrors hard to use.
You will not be able to brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It affects your steering.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire is dangerous because it affects your ability to steer. If your front tire goes flat while riding, safely leave the road as quickly as possible.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
Signal and check your mirrors.
Turn your head and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see if traffic is around you before changing lanes.

questions.question: If you shift to a lower gear while going too fast, what can happen?

options.text: The motorcycle may lurch and the rear tire may skid.
The motorcycle may accelerate too quickly.
The front tire will likely skid.
The engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle may lurch and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift to a lower gear while going too fast, the motorcycle will lurch and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: Brightly-colored helmets:

options.text: Can help other riders see you better.
Can be distracting.
Do not improve how visible you are.
Are not allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help other riders see you better.
questions.explanation: A brightly-colored helmet is a good choice. It protects your head in a crash and helps other drivers see you on the road.

questions.question: A proper lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you see others and be seen.
Help you avoid surface hazards.
Help you avoid traffic signals.
Show other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid traffic signals.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see and be seen. It helps you avoid hazards and wind from other vehicles. It also tells other drivers not to share your lane and gives you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle with a sidecar, the passenger should ride:

options.text: On the motorcycle seat.
In the sidecar.
Either on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.
Neither on the motorcycle nor in the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the sidecar.
questions.explanation: The passenger should ride in the sidecar. They must keep their hands inside the sidecar at all times.

questions.question: Which of the following gives a rider the best protection?

options.text: Goggles
A face shield
A windshield
Eyeglasses

questions.correctAnswerText: A face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield that resists breaking protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield or eyeglasses are not enough protection.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks that cross your lane at an angle, it is usually:

options.text: Safest to ride straight across the tracks within your lane.
Dangerous to ride straight across the tracks within your lane.
Not safe to cross tracks on a motorcycle.
Safest to cross the tracks by riding on the road shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safest to ride straight across the tracks within your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride straight across the tracks while staying in your lane. Do not turn to cross at a 90-degree angle, as this could move you into another lane.
